thesis.business_description: Hong Kong-listed (Bermuda-incorporated) investment holding company operating water supply, sewage treatment/environmental protection, and property businesses in mainland China; FY to March 2026 revenue HK$10,335.8m, down 11.3% ([HKEXnews results announcement](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0629/2026062900497.pdf), [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/utilities/hkg-855/china-water-affairs-group-shares/ownership)).
thesis.competitive_position: Regional water utility operator in mainland China with long-term concession-style assets, giving utility-type regulated returns; a mid-sized player rather than a national leader (no sourced market-share data). Profit attributable fell 8.2% to HK$986.2m and the final dividend was cut to HK13 cents from HK15 cents per a third-party summary ([Quartr](https://quartr.com/events/china-water-affairs-group-limited-855-h2-2026_F6dE6OcJ)). Moat is concession exclusivity; returns are constrained by tariff regulation (analyst judgement).
thesis.main_shareholders: Duan Chuanliang 27.18% (443,699,901 shares, 2 Oct 2024) and ORIX Corporation 19.75% (322,364,277 shares, 29 Feb 2024) per HKEX disclosure data shown on [etnet](https://content.etnet.com.hk/content/iq/compinfo/tc/quote_ci_brief.php?code=855); Simply Wall St shows about 27.5% and 25.5% respectively ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/utilities/hkg-855/china-water-affairs-group-shares/ownership)). Dates are old; check latest Form 2 filings.
thesis.red_flags: Refinancing pressure: offshore bank borrowings and other debt exceeding HK$4,000m were repayable within one year as of March 2026, and the company issued up to 130m warrants (HK$7.02 exercise) with about 90% of proceeds earmarked for debt repayment ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/hongkong/2026-05-12/china-water-affairs-plans-hk913m-warrant-issue-to-cut-debt), [iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1106958476)). Revenue fell 11.3% and dividend was cut ([HKEXnews](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0629/2026062900497.pdf)). An additional US$150m of 5.875% senior notes were issued in April 2026 to fund a tender offer on 2026 notes ([Minichart summary](https://www.minichart.com.sg/2026/06/29/china-water-affairs-group-2026-annual-results-revenue-profit-dividends-and-strategic-outlook/)).
thesis.insider_ownership: Duan Chuanliang 27.18% (2 Oct 2024) per [etnet](https://content.etnet.com.hk/content/iq/compinfo/tc/quote_ci_brief.php?code=855); his management role was not confirmed in the search results.

name: Shin Nippon Air Technologies Co., Ltd.

thesis.business_description: Tianneng Power International manufactures and sells lead-acid batteries (mainly for electric bicycles and other light electric vehicles) and has expanded into new-energy batteries and battery recycling/resource regeneration, with most revenue in mainland China ([Morningstar](https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/HKSE/00819)). FY2025 revenue was about RMB 53.8bn, down 29.83% ([HKEX results announcement](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0327/2026032703522.pdf)).
thesis.competitive_position: Company states its new-type lead-acid battery business ranks first in China (self-reported, no market share figure) ([ACN Newswire](https://www.acnnewswire.com/press-release/English/86137/Tianneng-Power's-Operatin)). Scale and a recycling loop for lead are the moat; exposure to commodity lead pricing and shifting regulation (battery standards, trade barriers) limits durability ([DCF-analysis PESTLE](https://dcf-analysis.com/products/0819hk-pestel-analysis), third-party). Revenue fell 51.5% in 1H25 with profit down 11.7% ([iTiger](https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1167644961)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Zhang Tianren about 36.6% (about 411.6m shares) per Simply Wall St aggregator; insiders 41.1% in total; other directors Zhang Kaihong, Shi Borong, Zhang Aogen each about 1.2-1.7% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/automobiles/hkg-819/tianneng-power-international-shares/ownership)). Aggregator data; HKEX filing not retrieved.
thesis.red_flags: Sharp revenue declines (FY2025 -29.83%; 1H25 -51.5%) with lead price/commodity volatility and heavy lead-based product exposure ([HKEX announcement](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0327/2026032703522.pdf); [PESTLE](https://dcf-analysis.com/products/0819hk-pestel-analysis)). Founder-family control (about 41% insiders) is a governance consideration. Environmental-regulation exposure inherent to lead processing (third-party).
thesis.insider_ownership: Zhang Tianren (Chairman) about 36.6%; insiders about 41.1% per Simply Wall St ([link](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/automobiles/hkg-819/tianneng-power-international-shares/ownership)).

name: The First Bank Of Toyama, Ltd.

thesis.business_description: Centurion Corporation (Singapore) owns and operates purpose-built workers accommodation (PBWA) and purpose-built student accommodation (PBSA) across Singapore, Malaysia, Australia, the UK and the US, and manages Centurion Accommodation REIT (CAREIT) ([SGX/CCL 1H FY2025 slides](https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/FHDWM3V6BYQSKK02/854733_CCL-Presentation%20Slides_1HFY2025%20Results-20250807.pdf)). FY2025 revenue was S$295.9m (+17%) and net profit S$141.6m (-63%; core operations profit +26% to S$139.2m) ([Minichart summary](https://www.minichart.com.sg/2026/02/26/centurion-corporation-fy2025-results-17-revenue-growth-sgd-4-0-cents-dividend-special-careit-distribution-announced/)).
thesis.competitive_position: Leading operator of Singapore dormitories (36,436 beds at 31 Mar 2025) and a large Malaysian portfolio (28,413 beds) ([SGX slides](https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/FHDWM3V6BYQSKK02/854733_CCL-Presentation%20Slides_1HFY2025%20Results-20250807.pdf)). Moat is scale, licensed sites and the REIT recycling platform, though dorm demand depends on foreign-worker quotas and student demand on visa policy; Australia PBSA occupancy fell to 93% from 96% ([POEMS](https://www.poems.com.sg/stocks/articles/centurion-corporation-fee-income-growth-mixed-results/)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Centurion Global Ltd about 51% (Simply Wall St, July 2025 analysis) with David Loh Kim Kang and Han Seng Juan as deemed holders; SGX change-of-interest notices filed 30 Mar 2026 ([SGX](https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/Z7QNPAMOB495KZPG/f47086ca4b7bf3c4e75cc0eb35e1602ad57bf08eb0fdb853595c56ed8ec4cb2e)). The Edge reported David Loh's total interest at 56.153% (undated) ([The Edge Singapore](https://testing.dev.theedgesingapore.com/capital/insider-moves/centurions-joint-chairman-loh-raises-stake-company)); current percentages not retrieved from the notices.
thesis.red_flags: Leverage: total debt about S$649.4m vs equity S$1.3bn (Simply Wall St, undated) while net gearing figures conflict (12% per Minichart vs 27% per POEMS) after the CAREIT spin-off ([POEMS](https://www.poems.com.sg/stocks/articles/centurion-corporation-fee-income-growth-mixed-results/)). Reported net profit fell 63% as prior-year gains did not recur. Controlling-holder concentration (over 50%) and related-party structure with the REIT/manager.
thesis.insider_ownership: Centurion Global Ltd about 51% and David Loh deemed interest total 56.153% (The Edge, undated); Han Seng Juan also a substantial shareholder per SGX notices of 30 Mar 2026.

thesis.business_description: Hong Kong-listed OEM/ODM manufacturer of plush stuffed toys, plastic figures, die-casting products and tarpaulin, with factories mainly in China and Vietnam; sells to brand owners and retailers, with North America (40.6% of 1H25 revenue), Japan (27.2%) and the PRC (19.7%) as the largest markets.
thesis.competitive_position: One of the world's largest plush toy manufacturers, also producing a large share of Funko Pops and key Spin Master plastic toys ([Asian Century Stocks](https://www.asiancenturystocks.com/deep-dive-2022-16-dream-international/)). Scale and quality control give a cost advantage over sub-scale family-run competitors and market-share gains despite a stagnant toy market ([Value Investors Club](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/Dream_International/1349679763)). Moat is customer integration and capacity, not pricing power: 1H26 revenue rose to about HK$2.9bn from HK$2.58bn but profit attributable fell to HK$205.9m from HK$307m on higher labour and raw material costs ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/hongkong/2026-08-26/dream-international-profit-drops-despite-rising-revenue); [RTTNews](https://www.rttnews.com/3684887/dream-international-h1-profit-falls.aspx)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Choi Kyoo Yoon (chairman/CEO) about 57.5%, Uni-Link Technology Limited about 10.7% and Fidelity International 9.94% per Simply Wall St (S&P data, updated June 2026) ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/consumer-durables/otc-drmm.f/dream-international/ownership)); aktien.guide citing filings dated 31 Dec 2025 shows Choi 57.50% and Uni-Link 10.66% ([aktien.guide](https://aktien.guide/stock-ownership/Dream-International-HK1126010854)). An etnet snapshot shows Choi 68.16% as of 30 Jun 2025, so figures vary ([etnet](https://etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ci_brief.php?code=1126)).
thesis.red_flags: Margin pressure: 1H26 profit down about 33% y/y on labour and raw-material cost increases, gross margin reportedly 15.4%, and management expects 2H26 to stay challenging amid trade barriers ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/hongkong/2026-08-26/dream-international-profit-drops-despite-rising-revenue)). Customer/geographic concentration: North America 40.6% and Japan 27.2% of 1H25 revenue; orders shifting to Vietnam to mitigate tariffs (same source family, 1H25 report). Controlling-holder dynamics: chairman holds a majority.
thesis.insider_ownership: Chairman and CEO Choi Kyoo Yoon about 57.5% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/consumer-durables/otc-drmm.f/dream-international/ownership); [aktien.guide](https://aktien.guide/stock-ownership/Dream-International-HK1126010854)).

thesis.business_description: Mitsui High-tec (Kitakyushu, Japan) makes precision stamping and processing products: electrical steel motor cores (for hybrid/EV traction motors), semiconductor lead frames, plus precision dies and other products, with plants in Japan, North America, Asia and Europe ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitsui_High-tec); [Quartr](https://quartr.com/events/mitsui-high-tec-inc-6966-q1-2027_F6ObSb1a)). FY1/2026 (Jan 2026) consolidated revenue was JPY 218.3bn ([JPX tanshin via search](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/69660/081220260311579530_tse-acedjpsm-69660-20260311369660-ixbrl.htm)).
thesis.competitive_position: Leading global motor-core maker, reported at about 40% of the global motor-core market in a 2022 Yomiuri report (via [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitsui_High-tec)); a third-party claim of over 70% is unverified. Moat is high-precision stamping/die know-how and customer qualification, while lead frames are exposed to cyclical semiconductor demand and precious-metal prices; Q1 FY2026 sales rose about 13% and operating profit about 28% on hybrid/EV demand ([Quartr](https://quartr.com/events/mitsui-high-tec-inc-6966-q1-2027_F6ObSb1a)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Mitsui Create Co., Ltd. 59,788 thousand shares (32.66%) as of Jan 2026 per ownership-table aggregator ([finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP%3A6966/ownership)); large-holding report cited at 29.74% (Sept 2024 amendment) ([kabuyoho](https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/report?bcode=6966)). Nomura Securities group large-holding report: 5.08% (Jul 2025), 3.86% (Mar 2026) ([kabutore](https://www.kabutore.biz/genzaikabuka/tairyohoyu.html?code=6966)).
thesis.red_flags: Thin net profit: FY1/2026 net income JPY 3.15bn on JPY 218.3bn revenue ([JPX tanshin via search](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/69660/081220260311579530_tse-acedjpsm-69660-20260311369660-ixbrl.htm)). Lead-frame segment faces delayed precious-metal price pass-through ([Quartr](https://quartr.com/events/mitsui-high-tec-inc-6966-q1-2027_F6ObSb1a)). Large capex for EV motor-core expansion (e.g. Ontario plant over CAD 100m, [Cornwall Seaway News](https://cornwallseawaynews.com/?p=70738)) exposes it to EV-demand swings. Controlling shareholder Mitsui Create holds about one-third.
thesis.insider_ownership: Mitsui Create (affiliated company; ownership by founding family/management not confirmed) 32.66% (Jan 2026); other individual insider holdings Not disclosed.

thesis.business_description: Hyundai Home Shopping Network (founded 2001, Seoul) is a Korean TV home shopping and e-commerce operator selling via cable, satellite and IPTV plus digital platforms, mainly in South Korea; it is part of the Hyundai Department Store Group ([Morningstar](https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/XKRX/057050)). Revenue is mostly sales commissions with limited inventory risk ([Value Investors Club](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/Hyundai_Home_Shopping_Network_Corp./1919536138), dated).
thesis.competitive_position: One of Korea's licensed TV home shopping operators within the Hyundai Department Store Group ecosystem; search results did not give market share or named rivals. Moat is the broadcast licence and group backing, offset by structural shift to online commerce (no quantified source found). The group chose to fold the listed company into its holding company to remove duplicate listing ([Daum/News1](https://v.daum.net/v/20260211145844180)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Hyundai G.F. Holdings held 6,882,852 shares (57.36%) before the share swap; the remainder except treasury (~6.6%) was to be acquired via comprehensive share exchange at 6.3571040 HGF shares per HSN share ([Daum](https://v.daum.net/v/20260211145844180)). Reported as 100% owned by Hyundai G.F. Holdings from 30 June 2026 ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/164537)).
thesis.red_flags: Delisting: company reported to have become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Hyundai G.F. Holdings via comprehensive share exchange and delisted in mid-2026 ([Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/article/2026072018093983123); [Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/164537)); no longer investable as a listed stock. Further plan reported to split into operating and investment companies.
thesis.insider_ownership: Controlled by Hyundai Department Store Group via Hyundai G.F. Holdings (100% after share swap) ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/164537)).

thesis.business_description: Myung In Pharmaceutical is a Korean specialty and generic pharmaceutical maker focused on central nervous system drugs (Parkinson's, schizophrenia, depression) plus OTC brands, in-licensing products such as Newron's evenamide and Luye's rivastigmine patch for Korea ([Business Wire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250109233767/en/newron-and-myung-in-pharm-announce-license-agreement-for-evenamide-in-south-korea)). 2025 consolidated revenue was KRW 287.3bn, operating profit KRW 92.5bn (32.2% margin) and net profit KRW 81.4bn ([HuffPost Korea](https://www.huffingtonpost.kr/article/256470); revenue also KRW 287.3bn per [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stock/kose/a317450)).
thesis.competitive_position: Self-described number one in the Korean CNS field (company claim, no independent share figure) ([Chemanager](https://chemanager-online.com/en/companies/myung-in-pharm/)). The very high 32% operating margin suggests pricing strength in its CNS niche, but moat rests on product registrations and doctor relationships; listed on KOSPI in Oct 2025 raising about KRW 197.2bn ([IPOX](https://www.ipox.com/ipo-calendar/myung-in-pharma)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Lee Haeng-myung (chairman) 7,428,000 shares (50.88% of 14.6m shares) as of 14 Oct 2025, falling to about 43.62% after gifts of 630,000 shares to elder daughter, 330,000 to younger daughter and 100,000 to a foundation ([DigitalToday](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/aigongsi/3715/lee-hang-myung-myeongin-pharmaceutical-stake-report); [Dailypharm](https://dailypharm.com/user/news/337244)). Owner family held about 96% before IPO and 74% after ([Newdaily](https://biz.newdaily.co.kr/site/data/html/2025/08/22/2025082200152.html)).
thesis.red_flags: Governance: criticism of a 'succession IPO' - chairman gifted about 1.06m shares to daughters/foundation shortly after IPO when the share price had fallen below the KRW 58,000 offer price; 2025 cash dividend KRW 21.9bn (about KRW 16.1bn to controlling holder and related parties) ([News Tomorrow/TF](https://news.tf.co.kr/read/economy/2326217.htm); [Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/162105)). Family-controlled with concentrated ownership (about 74% post-IPO, [Newdaily](https://biz.newdaily.co.kr/site/data/html/2025/08/22/2025082200152.html)). Allegations about a daughters-owned real-estate lessor (Medicommunication) are media claims.
thesis.insider_ownership: Lee Haeng-myung about 43.62% after gifts (50.88% before) ([DigitalToday](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/aigongsi/3715/lee-hang-myung-myeongin-pharmaceutical-stake-report)); daughters Lee Seon-young 4.32% and Lee Ja-young 2.26% via gifts.

thesis.business_description: Hong Kong-listed (Bermuda-incorporated) holding company whose main operating business is general insurance through Asia Insurance Company Limited in Hong Kong, plus portfolio investments; 2025 net profit attributable HK$1,053.0m (+62.7%) helped by a one-off gain on selling its stake in Hong Kong Life Insurance ([Insurance Business](https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/asia/news/breaking-news/asia-financial-reports-strong-growth-in-insurance-business-536505.aspx), [HKEXnews results](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0323/2026032300674.pdf)).
thesis.competitive_position: Established Hong Kong general insurer with regional ties to Japanese and Thai strategic holders (Sompo, Bangkok Bank, Aioi Nissay Dowa) ([etnet](https://www.etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ci_brief.php?code=662)); a niche local underwriter rather than a market leader (no sourced share). 2025 insurance revenue fell to HK$2,988.5m from HK$3,291.5m while insurance service expense rose to HK$2,827.8m from HK$2,461.3m, and the insurance operating result fell 51.0% to HK$181.3m ([HKEXnews](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0323/2026032300674.pdf)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Chan Charnwut Bernard and associates (via Claremont Capital Holdings) 62.83%, Sompo Holdings 9.93% (91,759,753 shares), Bangkok Bank 9.74% (89,988,236 shares) and Aioi Nissay Dowa Insurance 5.68% (52,550,175 shares), all as of 30 June 2025 ([etnet](https://www.etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ci_brief.php?code=662)); Simply Wall St shows Claremont at 61.2% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/insurance/hkg-662/asia-financial-holdings-shares/ownership)).
thesis.red_flags: Underwriting deterioration in 2025: insurance service expense up while insurance revenue fell, insurance operating result -51.0% ([HKEXnews](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0323/2026032300674.pdf)); headline 2025 profit growth relied on a one-off gain from the Hong Kong Life stake sale ([Insurance Business](https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/asia/news/breaking-news/asia-financial-reports-strong-growth-in-insurance-business-536505.aspx)). Controlling holder at about 62.8% limits free float.
thesis.insider_ownership: Chan Charnwut Bernard and associates 62.83% (via Claremont Capital Holdings) as of 30 June 2025 ([etnet](https://www.etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ci_brief.php?code=662)).

thesis.business_description: LX Semicon is a Korean fabless semiconductor company whose core products are display driver ICs (DDI) for OLED and LCD panels, plus timing controllers and power ICs, selling mainly to Korean display makers such as LG Display ([etnews](https://english.etnews.com/20220608200001); [Newsis](https://www.newsis.com/view/NISX20260601_0003651493)). 2Q26 revenue was KRW 401.2bn (+6% y/y) with operating profit KRW 22.0bn (+115%), helped by a one-off provision reversal ([Naver research report](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/61/20260728_company_146023000.pdf), via search summary).
thesis.competitive_position: Ranked third globally in DDI with an 11% share in 2021 (Omdia), behind Samsung System LSI and Novatek ([etnews](https://english.etnews.com/20220608200001)); no more recent share figure retrieved. Moat is design capability and entrenched LG Display relationship, but analysts flag limited growth from DDI alone due to LG Display restructuring and a North American customer diversifying DDI suppliers ([Alphasquare report](https://file.alphasquare.co.kr/media/pdfs/company-report/_26074529-108320.pdf)).
thesis.main_shareholders: LX Holdings (largest shareholder) 33.08% per Sept 2022 report ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/92387)) and LX Holdings plus 2 related persons 33.1% per April 2023 Kiwoom research ([Kiwoom report](https://files-scs.pstatic.net/2023/04/21/CmElb7VC9E/LX세미콘［108320］_20230421_Kiwoom_854370.pdf)); 2025 business-report holding not retrieved.
thesis.red_flags: Profit decline: operating profit fell for a second consecutive year and DDI market share loss hurt profitability ([Newsis](https://www.newsis.com/view/NISX20260601_0003651493)); 2026 operating profit forecast KRW 98.8bn (-9%) with gold-price cost pressure and LG Display Guangzhou LCD plant sale as variables ([Alphasquare report](https://file.alphasquare.co.kr/media/pdfs/company-report/_26074529-108320.pdf)). Customer concentration on LG Display (exact share not retrieved). Controlled by LX Holdings (about 33%).
thesis.insider_ownership: Controlled by LX Holdings (about 33.1%, dated 2023); individual management holdings Not disclosed in retrieved sources.

name: SBI Global Asset Management Co., Ltd.

thesis.business_description: Operator of the SOOP (formerly AfreecaTV, renamed Oct 2024) live-streaming platform in Korea with a Global arm, earning from virtual-gift donations, advertising and content. 1H26 revenue KRW 209.9bn, operating profit KRW 33.9bn.
thesis.competitive_position: Co-leader in Korean live streaming with Naver's CHZZK after Twitch exited Korea in Feb 2024; CHZZK reportedly reached 39% share by late 2025 ([Stream Hatchet](https://streamhatchet.com/blog/soop-afreecatvs-new-live-streaming-platform-fully-explained/)). In the latest month average viewers were similar (about 140k) but CHZZK led peak concurrents (800k vs 450k) ([Sidae](https://www.sidae.com/article/2026080313131118024)). Moat is streamer network effects, which are weak because streamers are portable; 2Q26 operating profit fell 57.9% year-on-year to KRW 12.6bn ([InvenGlobal](https://www.invenglobal.com/articles/21491/soop-announces-q1-2026-results-revenue-of-106-billion-operating-profit-of-212-billion); [Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/166405)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Saint International and 6 related persons 25.88% (Nov 2025 broker report); foreign ownership 31.84% ([Kyobo Securities report](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/34/20251103_company_979607000.pdf)). Saint International is 85% owned by CEO Seo Su-gil ([Bizwatch](https://news.bizwatch.co.kr/article/mobile/2025/02/20/0024)).
thesis.red_flags: 2Q26 profit hit by one-time costs from a tax audit and strategic investment ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/166405)); Android app-market removal and iOS in-app payment exclusion hit 4Q25 donation revenue; competition from CHZZK; Meritz cut target price to KRW 76,000 from 83,000 ([Sidae](https://www.sidae.com/article/2026080313131118024)). Controlling-holder dynamics: effective control by CEO via a personal holding company.
thesis.insider_ownership: CEO Seo Su-gil owns 85% of Saint International, which holds 25%+ of SOOP; with related persons 25.88% ([Bizwatch](https://news.bizwatch.co.kr/article/mobile/2025/02/20/0024); [Kyobo report](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/34/20251103_company_979607000.pdf)).

thesis.business_description: Singapore-listed investment holding company distributing and retailing luxury timepieces and accessories (including Patek Philippe and Rolex boutiques) in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand, with a smaller wholesale segment. 1H FY2026 (to 30 Sep 2025) revenue S$468.7m, of which Singapore S$191.1m and rest of Southeast Asia S$201.6m.
thesis.competitive_position: Regional luxury watch retailer/distributor with flagship boutiques, e.g. a Patek Philippe duplex boutique at One Bangkok described as the brand's first in Southeast Asia ([Cortina Annual Report 2026](https://www.cortinawatch.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/CHL-Annual-Report-2026_compressed-1.pdf)). Moat is brand-principal relationships and boutique locations, which depend on continued brand support; 1H FY2026 profit rose 10.6% to S$34.4m but gross margin slipped to 31.8% and opex rose 13.3% ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1103250564)). Management cites softer consumer sentiment and macro uncertainty in FY2026.
thesis.main_shareholders: Lim family via Lim Keen Ban Holdings: 32.768% after a married deal of 1.6m shares at S$3.80 (undated, up from 31.802%) per [The Edge Singapore](https://alfi.dev.theedgesingapore.com/capital/insider-moves/cortinas-lim-family-raises-stake-married-deal-substantial-shareholder-union); Simply Wall St shows Lim Keen Ban Holdings at 34.7% (undated) ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/sg/retail/sgx-c41/cortina-holdings-shares/ownership)).
thesis.red_flags: Margin pressure: 1H FY2026 gross margin 31.8% and opex +13.3% ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1103250564)).
